_README: TEMPLATE ONLY. Not deployed, not published, not served.
This is the client-metadata document Spotify's authorization server would
fetch when it receives this URL as OAuth client_id (SEP-991 CIMD).
BLOCKED until: (1) an HTTPS host serves this at a stable, public URL with a
non-root path, and (2) that URL is added to the Portal allowed-client-pattern
list. The allow-list gate is PROVEN, not assumed - see STATE.md section 16.
STEP 1 - choose the CIMD URL, then STEP 2 - compute the redirect port.
The port is NOT free to choose. mcp-remote derives it:
hash = md5(serverUrl + '|' + resource + '|' + clientMetadataUrl)
The hash INCLUDES this document's own URL, so the URL must be fixed first.
Worked examples already computed:
https://kooshapari.com/oauth/client-metadata.json -> port 18586
https://jcode.sh/oauth/client-metadata.json      -> port 35683
Reproduce with: python3 scripts/derive_callback_port.py <cimd-url>
STEP 3 - replace <CIMD_URL>, <PORT>, <CLIENT_NAME> below, publish the file
over HTTPS with content-type application/json, then request the pattern be
added to Portal's allowed clients.
HOSTING (verified 2026-10-15, see PORTAL-FINDINGS.md):
Do NOT use https://kooshapari.com/oauth/client-metadata.json - returns 404.
Do NOT use https://jcode.sh/oauth/client-metadata.json - returns HTTP 200 but
content-type text/html, 98237 bytes. jcode.sh is a Cloudflare SPA that serves
the HTML shell with 200 for EVERY path, so that 200 is a fallback, not a
document. Always check content-type on an SPA host.
Viable: commit this file to a public repo and serve via raw.githubusercontent.com
(KooshaPari/Jcode is public and raw fetches work anonymously). CAVEAT: raw
serves JSON as content-type text/plain. Whether Spotify's auth backend accepts
that is NOT established. If it is strict, use a static host or Cloudflare Worker
that returns application/json instead.
Preferred: a Cloudflare Worker returning application/json at a stable path.
PORT DEPENDS ON THE URL. Already computed:
https://kooshapari.com/oauth/client-metadata.json -> 18586
https://jcode.sh/oauth/client-metadata.json      -> 35683
(any other host gives a different port; re-derive, never copy)
IDENTITY: client_name must be our own. Do NOT copy Xirp's
client-metadata.json URL as the client_id. That URL is allow-listed and
would authenticate AS Xirp, attributing Jcode's actions to Xirp in
Portal's audit trail.
UNRESOLVED - raise with vendor: mcp-remote builds its callback as
http://127.0.0.1:<port>/oauth/callback, but the allow-listed Xirp document
declares http://127.0.0.1/callback (default port, different path). If the
server compares redirect_uri strictly, the derived port must be registered
and the Xirp form would not match. Confirm before publishing.
